PARKS, RECREATION & COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

Welcome to the meeting of the Parks, Recreation & Community Services Commission. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast
throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs and videotapes of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office by calling
(818) 548-2090. Meetings are also archived on the City website for viewing anytime at www.ci.glendale.ca.us/video_archives.asp.
PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES AND PAGERS WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request.
Assisted listening devices are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for requests regarding sign language
translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
are public records, will be available for review in the Community Services & Parks Administration Office, 613 E. Broadway, Room 120, Glendale, CA 91206. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact (818) 548-2782 during regular business hours.

  MEETING AGENDA
  Monday, September 16, 2019, 2:30 p.m.
  Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206
1.  ROLL CALL
  A. Report of Recording Clerk, re: Posting of the Agenda. The Agenda for the September 16, 2019,
  regular meeting was posted on the bulletin board outside City Hall on or before Friday, September
  13, 2019.
2.  UPCOMING COUNCIL AGENDA ITEMS
3.  COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to items not a part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five (5) minutes. The
  Commission may question the speaker, but there will be no debate or decision. The Director may refer
  the matter to the proper section for investigation and report.
5.  CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the Commission or
  audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such request before a motion is
  proposed.
  A.  Approval of the Minutes of the Commission regular meeting held on August 19, 2019.
6.  REPORTS – INFORMATION ONLY
  A. Capital Improvement Program (CIP) Update
  B. Section Activity Reports
  1.  Recreation & Community Services
  2.  Park Services

7.  ADJOURNMENT
  NEXT MEETING:
  October 21, 2019 – City Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway
minutes_text:
PARKS, RECREATION & COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

  MEETING MINUTES
  Monday, September 16, 2019, 2:30 p.m.
  Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206
1.  ROLL CALL

  The meeting was called to order at 2:36 p.m.

  Present: Commissioners Eberle, Kalfayan, Michals, and President Pro-Tem Wolfson
  Absent: Babaian

  A.  Report of Recording Clerk, re: Posting of the Agenda. Ms. Moreno Hernandez reported that the
  agenda for the September 16, 2019, regular meeting was posted on the bulletin board outside City
  Hall on or before Friday, September 13, 2019.
2.  UPCOMING COUNCIL AGENDA ITEMS
  Director of Community Services & Parks Onnig Bulanikian read a list of upcoming City Council agenda
  items related to the Community Services & Parks Department (CSP).

3.  COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
  Commissioner Kalfayan asked for an update on the renovation of Fremont Park, which Mr. Bulanikian
  provided.

  Commissioner Eberle asked for more information regarding the master plan. Deputy Director
  Panossian said that he would be giving an overview of the project during agenda item 6A and could
  also email the master plan to Commissioner Eberle so that she could zoom in on the image.

  Ms. Moreno Hernandez announced upcoming events organized or sponsored by the Community
  Services & Parks Department.

4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Speakers:
  1. Diana Walker, Real Estate Agent – Glenoaks Park
  2. Audry Zarokian, GOCHA Board Member – Glenoaks Park
5.  CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  A. Approval of the Minutes of the Commission regular meeting held on August 19, 2019.

  Moved:  Commissioner Kalfayan
  Seconded: Commissioner Eberle

  That the minutes of the Commission regular meeting held on August 19, 2019, be approved
  as written.

  A roll call was conducted and Commissioners voted as follows:

  1
   Ayes:  Commissioners Eberle, Kalfayan, Michals, and President Pro-Tem Wolfson
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioners Babaian
  Abstain:  None

6.  REPORTS – INFORMATION ONLY
  A. Capital Improvement Program (CIP) Update
  Deputy Director Koko Panossian gave a PowerPoint presentation covering the following capital
  improvement projects: Glendale Narrows Riverwalk Phase II, Maple Park’s All-Inclusive
  Playground, Central Library Demonstration Garden, Sports Complex Concession Building
  Renovations, Fremont Park Renovation, Central Park Master Plan, Cerritos Elementary School
  Multi-Purpose Field, Wilson Middle School Multi-Purpose Field, Glendale High School Tennis
  Courts, Deukmejian Barn Nature Education Center Interior Improvements and Restroom Building,
  Lower School Restroom and Picnic Area Rehabilitation, Nibley Park Rehabilitation, Pacific Park
  Shade and Water Play, Upper Scholl Canyon Ball Field Concession/Restroom Building
  Renovation, Verdugo Park North Renovation, Pacific Park Artificial Turf Project, Montrose Park
  Parking Resurfacing, and Dunsmore Parking Lot Resurfacing.

  Commissioners asked about tables at Fremont Park, U-12 vs. U-14 fields, the location of Heritage
  Garden, and marketing of joint-use facilities.

  B.  Section Activity Reports
  1.  Recreation & Community Services
  Deputy Director Tereza Aleksanian gave a PowerPoint presentation covering the following
  topics: National Night Out, Summer Concerts in the Park, Maple Park All-Inclusive Playground
  Grand Opening, Summer Luau Celebration, Therapeutic Recreation, Youth & Family Services,
  S.T.A.R. End of Summer Barbeque, S.T.A.R. Graffiti Removal, and Trails and Open Space
  Workdays and Campfire Program.

  2.  Park Services
  Mr. Panossian provided a brief overview of work orders completed by Park Services staff in
  the month of August and gave a PowerPoint presentation highlighting projects at: Verdugo
  Road – Sparr Heights District sign, Verdugo Park Ballfield, Carr Park, Heritage Garden, Pacific
  Park, and Brand Park.
7.  ADJOURNMENT
  The meeting was adjourned at 3:58 p.m.
